chunks.rationale: electron/test/services.test.js is the contract: addProject git-inits a plain directory, leaves existing files, and surfaces `Could not initialize a git repository` instead of the old 'Not a git repository' toast. The two former reject-non-git tests were the bug the screenshot hit. projects-create.test.js still proves Create new mkdir + work tree via the shared addProject init. webDegrade checks the existing-mode note.
risks: The init-failure test stubs only `git init` and lets real `git rev-parse` run. A full git-missing stub would skip the init branch if isInsideWorkTree treated every git error as 'not a repo' (it does) and then fail init — that path is covered. A stub that makes rev-parse succeed on a non-repo would skip init entirely; we do not fake that.
Renderer tests use fakeCoder and never actually git-init.

chunks.rationale: electron/services.js ensureGitWorkTree: if the local folder is not already a work tree, `git init -q` then re-check. addProject calls it after the directory exists check. createProject is now mkdir + addProject with rm -rf rollback on any add failure, so there is one init path.
risks: Picking a parent like ~/code that is not itself a repo will git-init that parent. Same class of mistake as adding the wrong folder; we do not scan for nested repos.
A folder already inside another git work tree (`rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` true) is added as-is and is NOT inited. That is existing behavior.
Bare repos still fail the post-init work-tree check. Nested .git file (submodule gitfile) is treated as already a work tree if rev-parse says so.
No initial commit. Worktree threads on a freshly inited repo still need a HEAD; default + thread is checkout-bound so first-run is OK.
createProject rollback now deletes the new folder on ANY addProject failure, not just init. That is stricter than before and correct for a folder we just created.

chunks.rationale: AddProjectPathModal existing-mode copy: placeholder is a folder path, plus a one-line note that we will git-init if needed. CSS fieldNote is muted 12px, matching fieldError metrics. SSH remotes are unchanged and skip ensureGitWorkTree.
risks: addViaDialog still goes through addProject, so the native leftover picker also inits. Fine.
The toast in the screenshot came from useCoder.addProject catch (setError) because addProject threw. After this, a successful init returns the project and clears the error.

chunks.rationale: The reported failure: merge blocked on '.solenta/review-itinerary.json + AGENTS.md'. tryResolveItineraryOnly only fired when the itinerary was the SOLE unmerged path, so any second app-generated file (config-doctor AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md) sent the user to hand-resolve in the worktree. Now each unmerged path is classified: itinerary -> combine both sides (unchanged logic), config-doctor output -> checkout --ours, anything else -> bail, exactly as before.
risks: Auto-taking ours on a generated doc drops the other side's regeneration; safe because the file is a projection of shared memory and the next doctor run rewrites it whole.
Gate is the GENERATED_MARKER present in BOTH stages :2 and :3 — a hand-authored AGENTS.md still conflicts (second test covers this).

chunks.rationale: Same helper is used by mergeWorktree, mergeInto's squash and replay, updatePrBranchFromBase and the PR-update path; renaming in place keeps one shared resolution policy instead of per-caller guards. New require of ./configDoctor.js is leaf-only (fs/path), no cycle.
risks: mergeInto squash site runs in the project checkout, where --ours = the target branch — intended.

chunks.rationale: Two cases: generated AGENTS.md + itinerary conflicting together now merges clean; hand-authored AGENTS.md still throws MERGE_CONFLICT.
